newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse allows reference price to float.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse allows reference price to float.

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange said on Tuesday it would allow its stocks' reference prices to fluctuate within a plus/minus 50 percent corridor, up from a present 10 percent margin, starting with Wednesday's session.

It said the move -- tested on first-tier fertiliser maker Azomures on Tuesday -- was in line with commercial banks' higher interest rates on deposits and with the continuous depreciation of the leu currency.
"We started with Azomures as the company is highly liquid and trades in heavy volumes," exchange general manager Stere Farmache said.
Brokers were divided on the effects of the new corridor.
"This is something that will keep small investors away from the market," one said.
Another said: "The decision is wise and comes at a time when the market has gained in volume. It was necessary given the fall of the leu, as otherwise investors would have lost in real terms."
The leu fell by around 120 percent since January to an interbank rate of 9,000 against the dollar.
"We needed the move as due to the low 10 percent margin transactions got easily blocked," Farmache said.
The reference rate is a weighted average of all the prices at which deals for a particular stock were struck in a previous session.

"Don't forget the OTC market, where prices can float freely. With a 10 percent margin, investors would have migrated on to the RASDAQ," a trader said in reference to Romania's over-the-counter system RASDAQ, opened last October.
